Using the correct Law of Cosines at \(F\):

\[
PE^2=EF^2+PF^2-2(EF)(PF)\cos\angle EFP
\]

\[
9=49+25-70\cos\angle EFP \Rightarrow \cos\angle EFP=\frac{13}{14}
\]

Set \(F=(0,0)\), \(P=(5,0)\), so \(A=(6.5,0)\). Since

\[
\sin\angle EFP=\sqrt{1-\left(\frac{13}{14}\right)^2}=\frac{3\sqrt3}{14},
\]

and \(EF=7\),

\[
E=\left(7\cdot \frac{13}{14},7\cdot \frac{3\sqrt3}{14}\right)=\left(\frac{13}{2},\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}\right).
\]

Thus \(A\) and \(E\) have the same \(x\)-coordinate, so triangles \(EPA\) and \(EAF\) are right at \(A\). Their circumcenters are midpoints of hypotenuses:

\[
O_1=\text{midpoint of }PE=\left(\frac{23}{4},\frac{3\sqrt3}{4}\right)
\]

\[
O_2=\text{midpoint of }EF=\left(\frac{13}{4},\frac{3\sqrt3}{4}\right)
\]

Therefore,

\[
d=\left|\frac{23}{4}-\frac{13}{4}\right|=\frac{5}{2}
\]

\[
2d=5
\]

\[
\boxed{5}
\]
